title: CounterStereotypicalAttributes
description: One judge's assessment of one report against the Path A rubric. reportId is attached by the pipeline rather than echoed by the model, so a model can never mislabel which report it judged. Each attribute carries a third outcome, "insufficient_evidence", which is recorded separately from a negative judgment: the reports differ in how much archived publisher text survives, and a judge that cannot see enough to decide must say so rather than guess. The two binary attributes are written out in full rather than shared through $defs, and nullability uses anyOf rather than a type array, so that the same file is accepted verbatim by both providers' structured-output validators.

typicality.description: Whether the actor is presented as an ordinary member of their group.

judgment.description: "yes" or "no" is a decision about this report. "insufficient_evidence" means the text you were given does not let you decide either way; it is not a negative judgment and is never a failure.

evidence.description: Verbatim span from the text you were given, under 200 characters. Empty string when the text contains nothing bearing on this judgment.

heterogeneity.description: Whether the report explicitly signals that this is not a single individual.

violation.description: How far the depicted position departs from the partisan stereotype.

level.description: Only "moderate" counts toward the score; the relationship is an inverted U. "none" is a decision that the depicted position does not depart from the stereotype; "insufficient_evidence" means the text does not let you place the departure at all. Do not use "none" for the latter.

prototype.description: Descriptive content type. Does not affect the attribute judgments.
